task.title: Grade book
task.description: The platform sets an array students of objects { name, score }. Write pure functions that do not change the input array: getAverage(list) - the average score rounded with Math.round, 0 for an empty array; getExcellentNames(list) - an array of the names of students with a score of 90 or more; findStudent(list, name) - the student object or undefined; addStudent(list, name, score) - a new array with the added { name, score }. Use reduce, filter, map, find and spread ...

tests.name: getAverage(students) = 83 (82.5 rounded)
tests.fail: Sum with reduce, divide by list.length, round with Math.round.

tests.name: getAverage on another array: 70 and 81 → 76
tests.fail: Calculate from the list parameter, not from students.

tests.name: getAverage([]) = 0
tests.fail: For an empty array division gives NaN - return 0 in advance: if (list.length === 0) { return 0; }

tests.name: getExcellentNames(students) → ["Anna", "Sardor"]
tests.fail: filter by score >= 90, then map((student) => student.name).

tests.name: Boundary: 90 points is a top student
tests.check: JSON.stringify(getExcellentNames([{ name: "Ira", score: 90 }, { name: "Oleg", score: 89 }])) === JSON.stringify(["Ira"])

tests.name: getExcellentNames([]) → []
tests.fail: An empty array gives an empty array if you use filter and map.

tests.name: findStudent returns undefined if there is no such student
tests.fail: find returns undefined by itself - filter would return an array.

tests.name: addStudent returns a new array with the student
tests.check: (() => { const next = addStudent(students, "Ira", 88); return next.length === 5 && next[4].name === "Ira" && next[4].score === 88 && next !== students; })()

tests.name: addStudent does not change the original array
tests.check: (() => { const before = JSON.stringify(students); addStudent(students, "Ira", 88); return JSON.stringify(students) === before; })()
tests.fail: push changes the original array. Create a new one: [...list, ...].

tests.name: reduce, filter, map, find and ... are used
tests.fail: Solve the task with array methods, without hand-written loops.

tests.name: The program runs without errors
tests.fail: There is an error in the code - read its text in the console.

hints: Sum: list.reduce((sum, student) => sum + student.score, 0) - do not forget 0.
New array: [...list, { name, score }] - short for { name: name, score: score }.

wrong_solutions.mistake: no check for an empty array

questions.question: const a = ["x", "y", "z"]; What does a[1] return?
How do you get the last item of the array arr? Type the expression.
What does this print: const cart = []; cart.push("cheese"); console.log(cart.length);
options: An error: cart is a constant
questions.explanation: const forbids reassigning the variable, not changing the array's contents.

questions.question: Match the method with what it returns.
pairs: A new array of the same length
A new array with the matching items
questions.explanation: None of them changes the original array.

questions.question: What does [5, 12, 8, 20].filter((n) => n > 10) return?
questions.explanation: filter keeps the items for which the function returned true.

questions.question: What is [3, 4, 5].reduce((sum, n) => sum + n, 0)? Type the number.
Which ways of reading the name property of the user object are correct?
questions.explanation: A dot or square brackets with a string; JavaScript has no ->.

questions.question: What does [{ id: 1 }, { id: 2 }].find((x) => x.id === 3) return?
questions.explanation: If nothing is found, find returns undefined.

questions.question: Which operations change the original array?
questions.explanation: map and filter return a new array.

questions.question: What does this print: const user = { name: "Anna", age: 15 }; const { age } = user; console.log(age);
questions.explanation: Destructuring creates a constant age with the value user.age.

questions.question: Match the expression with the result when const a = [1, 2].
questions.explanation: Spread puts the items into a new array.
